title: Diagnostic Information for Student Retention and Success (DMISRS) Project
text:
The DMISRS Project is a collaborative project which aims to analyse the curricula of first year Mathematics courses in Higher Education in order to establish how best to address students’ needs through curriculum-integrated support initiatives, including blended-learning.
Individual areas of need for students in identified institutions are determined through NSC Mathematics and NBT sub-domain analysis and the kind of Mathematics support needed are workshopped.
The project benefit academics, institutions and students in the following ways:

It enables academics to leverage the diagnostic potential of the provided information in addressing the needs of their particular students.
Individual student reports enable students to review where they are in their learning and enable academics to address the mathematical diversity in a programme or course rather than follow a one-size-fits-all approach to teaching and learning.
The information resulting from the analysis could be used by institutions as a tool for student placement and support and to establish curriculum-integrated support initiatives.
It enables academics to make evidence-based decisions for curriculum change to enhance student success.
It enhances curriculum support in Mathematics to increase student participation and success in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) programmes.
It has the potential to change the profile of students succeeding in Mathematics and STEM programmes.
It aims to enhance the first year experience and to reduce attrition.
